stackfacts/keywords: check my stack for end-of-life versions and exploited CVEs
EOL, package vulnerabilities and KEV in one call

description: Check dependencies, runtimes and OS versions in one call: OSV for up to 50 purls, EOL for 50 product@version pairs, CISA KEV hits, suggestions for unknowns.

cves.description: Optional CVE ids to check against CISA KEV; duplicates are merged. Leave out (or send []) to check versions only

items.description: The versions to check, in order: "product@version" strings or {product, version} objects. Needed unless packages is sent. Send each item as one string, product@version, e.g. {"items":["nodejs@18.19.0"]}

product.description: endoflife.date product id or alias, e.g. nodejs, python, ubuntu (GET /v1/eol/index lists them)

version.description: Version string, e.g. 18.19.0 (send "3.10" as a string, not a number)

packages.description: Optional package URLs with versions, answered as POST /v1/osv/check answers them (advisories, fixed versions, KEV flag). Types: npm, pypi, golang, cargo, maven (nuget, gem and composer are answered as ecosystem_unavailable until imported)

items.description: purl with a version, e.g. pkg:npm/lodash@4.17.20 or pkg:maven/org.apache.logging.log4j/log4j-core@2.14.1

name: stackfacts_stack_check
